Only 1,610 of those 3,237 have the same contract stored on the next trading day. The ingest_jobs table shows the two ATM +/- 40 backfill jobs ran with options excluded: ingest_queue holds only spot (501) and fut (1,447) tasks, all done. Timing test: a directional credit spread (signal on 1d: close > EMA20 and EMA20 rising -> bull put spread, short 100 pts OTM / long 300 pts OTM; mirror -> bear call; nearest weekly with min_days 3; target 50% / stop 100% of credit on net P&L; exit on opposite signal; max 3 days) ran in 5 s but produced 11 trades out of ~233 signal days: skipped 222, missing_data 234. The 11 trades that did run (net +4.2k, PF 1.35, t 0.41, net_ex_top_k +0.3k, H1 +8.6k / H2 -4.3k) are a biased sample: they are exactly the strikes that earlier experiments happened to fetch, which correlates with where the index went later (a form of lookahead). So I ran no grid and submit no candidates: any result on this data would be selection bias, not an edge. Side check on daily candles 2015-2025 (no options, no test-window data): the same EMA20 trend signal has no 3-day directional edge (mean move in the signal direction from next open to the 3rd close -0.016%, t about -0.3; 2025 -0.125%; adverse move > 0.4% in 41% of 2025 signals). A trend-direction credit spread would therefore rely on premium decay alone, which earlier cycles found didn't hold up out of sample. Debit spreads on daily breakouts have the same issue: no directional edge in the signal.
platform_issues: DATA: the brief says 'NIFTY / SENSEX weekly options, ATM +/- 40 strikes, nearest 2 weeklies, 2025-01 -> 2026-10-26' are stored. They aren't. In the snapshot, 2025 has about 13 NIFTY option contract-days per trading day, nearest weekly only (e.g. fetch_log for 2025-06-10 has 10 contracts, all on the 12 Jun expiry), and 2026 has about 20 a day (4,060 contract-days). Reproduce with: select count(*) from fetch_log where kind='opt' and underlying='NIFTY' and status='ok' and day between '2025-01-01' and '2025-12-31' -> 3237. ingest_jobs 24cb8e130b and aab7b71ec3 ('band 40, expiries_ahead 2') queued only spot/fut tasks, so they look like they were planned with include_options=False. Any cycle-4 option family is blocked until options are backfilled. Rough cost of the backfill: 2025 alone, +/- 40 strikes x 2 rights x 2 weeklies is about 80k contract-days, about 40k Breeze calls (2 weekdays per call), about 10 days at the 4,000/day budget. A +/- 10-strike band is about a quarter of that (about 2.5 days).

Screen summary: 'missing_data' and 'skipped' are reported but nothing warns or fails. A spec where 95% of signals are skipped still returns a normal-looking summary (PF, t, win rate). A warning (or refusing to compute t / PF) when skipped / (trades + skipped) > ~10% would stop biased screens from being read as results.
